gap: No result ChatGPT got states the screens on one scale: pixels added and pixel density per screen, brightness in one unit, and gamut claims converted ("72% NTSC" and "100% sRGB" are the same area claim). On that scale the FOPO S7 adds 4.61 MP at 162 PPI and 3.55 lb for two screens, about 2.2 times the pixels of the $80–110 single 1080p extenders the rivals rank, but at 250 nits against their 280–300.
standout_why: Compared against The Office Journal under-$200 and under-$150 (both cited), itechguides 2025 (cited) and our own under-$300 page (rank 10). All four print raw listing figures; none gives PPI, megapixels added or a gamut conversion, and none puts FOPO's 250 cd/m² beside the 280–300 nits of the Amazon-brand rows. The Office Journal prints "72% NTSC" for one row and "72% sRGB" for the next without comment. The one-video-output-per-screen rule is already on our under-$300 page, so it is not new. DeskFinds (rank 1 in the first chat, not cited) returned HTTP 403, so I could not check it. The table is half-built: FOPO, Mobile Pixels and Arzopa store pages returned HTTP 429 on every try, so the S1, Fold, Glance, UPERFECT, SideTrak and Arzopa rows are not verified.
decides: It confirms a split answer and does not overturn a pick. For two added screens under $200, the FOPO S7 is denser and lighter than the ZUMWALT P7 that The Office Journal ranks (162 vs 141 PPI, 3.55 vs 4 lb, 4.61 vs 4.15 MP) but dimmer by the makers' figures (250 vs 280 nits) and smaller (14 vs 15.6 inch). For one added screen, the sharpness that ChatGPT's first pick trades on (UPERFECT 14-inch 2240×1400) is a pixel-density lead that no row we link under $200 matches; I could not open a page for that resolution, so the lead stays out of the findings. Each S7 screen needs its own video output, so a base M1, M2 or M3 MacBook drives only one of the two.

findings.label: Normalised: pixels added, density, weight per screen, brightness

findings.note: Arithmetic on the figures above. Diagonal pixels √(1920² + 1200²) = 2,264.2; ÷ 14 in = 161.7 PPI. 1920 × 1200 = 2,304,000 px per screen. 1.61 kg × 2.2046 = 3.55 lb. 1 cd/m² = 1 nit.

findings.note: "Triple" here means two added screens. The page gives "about $190 at the time of writing" (dated 2026-09-11) and says its comparison is from published specs, not testing. √(1920² + 1080²) = 2,202.9; ÷ 15.6 = 141.2 PPI. 2 × 2,073,600 px = 4.15 MP. No price was read today.

findings.label: Gamut claims on one scale
findings.value: sRGB's area is 0.72 of NTSC's, so "72% NTSC" (ROYY, KEFEYA) and "100% sRGB" (Vixtan) are the same area claim; neither proves full sRGB coverage
findings.source_title: What is Color Gamut? (BenQ Knowledge Center)
findings.note: BenQ: "the area ratio of sRGB to NTSC is 0.72 to 1" and "we cannot say 72% NTSC color gamut is equal to sRGB color gamut", because area is not coverage. BenQ is a monitor maker. The gamut strings come from the two rival pages in the next finding and the itechguides page.
